key_concepts: Observing is the most basic science process skill.
Observing uses the five senses: sight, smell, hearing, taste, and touch.
Observing gathers information from the surroundings.
Predicting is using observations to tell what will happen next.
A candle burns longer as the size of the covering jar increases.
Some objects float in water while others sink.
A small coin sinks in water, so a large coin is also likely to sink.
Measuring length can be done using a ruler or meterstick.
A standard ruler has centimeter and inch scales, with millimeter as the smallest unit.
A meterstick is easier to use than a ruler for measuring height.
Science process skills include observing, predicting, and measuring.
